note: One original write-up per High-confidence selection. Every factual clause is traceable to the official page named in the row; no form claim is made that the source does not print.

predictions.text: Back Edinburgh to beat the Lions at Hive Stadium on Friday. The official URC match centre records Edinburgh's most recent match as a 29-12 win away at Zebre Parma, while the Lions were beaten 57-15 by the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld in the same round. Edinburgh therefore arrive with a seventeen-point road win behind them and face opponents who lost by forty-two points last time out. The selection is the Edinburgh moneyline at our 1.40.

The selection is the Bulls moneyline at 1.40 against Ulster at Loftus Versfeld. The URC match centre lists the Bulls' Round 3 result as a 57-15 win over the Lions in Pretoria, a forty-two point margin, while Ulster were held to a 26-26 draw by Munster at the Affidea Stadium. A side that has just won by forty-two points at home, against opponents who could not close out a home draw, is our highest-rated rugby union pick of the round.

Take the Stormers to beat the Scarlets at DHL Stadium. The official URC record shows the Stormers beating the Sharks 39-22 in Cape Town in Round 3, a seventeen-point win, while the Scarlets needed a one-point margin to edge Benetton 27-26 at Parc y Scarlets. That verified margin, plus home advantage in Cape Town, is why the Stormers moneyline at 1.40 is the pick for this fixture.

Leinster at 1.40 is the pick for the Aviva Stadium meeting with Munster. The URC match centre records Leinster's Round 3 as a 29-5 win over Cardiff in Dublin, a twenty-four point margin, while Munster were pegged back to a 26-26 draw at Ulster. Leinster also have the venue: this one is at the Aviva Stadium, and the model rates the home side 0.82 to win.

Ospreys to win at St Helen's is the selection. They beat the Dragons 38-31 at Rodney Parade in Round 3, a seven-point away win recorded on the official URC match centre, so they have already shown they can outscore this opponent on the road. The fixture now returns to St Helen's, and the model lifts the Ospreys to roughly 0.72 with home advantage applied. The moneyline at 1.40 is the bet.

Back Tonga to beat Lebanon at CommBank Stadium. The official Rugby League World Cup site records Tonga's Round 1 as a 30-12 win over England at HBF Park in Perth, an eighteen-point margin, while Lebanon lost 42-18 to Papua New Guinea in Port Moresby. Those two verified scorelines are the entire input: Tonga carry a plus-eighteen margin into this pool B fixture and Lebanon a minus twenty-four, which is why the Tonga moneyline at 1.40 is the desk's strongest league pick of the week.

England are the pick to beat France at HBF Park. England lost their opener 12-30 to Tonga in Perth, but France's Round 1 was a 4-78 defeat by Samoa at CommBank Stadium, the heaviest margin of the tournament so far. The pool B table therefore separates them by sixty-two points of verified differential, and England also return to the Perth venue where they played last week. The selection is the England moneyline at 1.40.

Samoa to win in Port Moresby is the call. Samoa opened the World Cup with a 78-4 win over France in Sydney, a seventy-four point margin, while Papua New Guinea beat Lebanon 42-18 at the Santos National Football Stadium, the venue for this one. Even allowing for the Kumuls' home crowd and the fact that both ratings rest on a single match, Samoa's verified differential is far larger, so the Samoa moneyline at 1.42 is the selection.

New Zealand at 1.40 to beat the Cook Islands in Christchurch. The Kiwis' only verified result is a 24-22 loss to Australia at Allianz Stadium, a two-point game against the tournament hosts, whereas the Cook Islands were beaten 40-12 by Fiji in Newcastle. New Zealand now play at One NZ Stadium with a twenty-six point swing in verified margin, so the home moneyline is the selection despite the narrow opening defeat.
